verified_signals.entity: Albanian Tax Administration (DPT) / 2025 tax-procedures amendments (POS/POI mandate)
verified_signals.signal: Albania has a universal legal obligation for taxpayers to be equipped with POS/POI card-acceptance terminals at every point of sale. The Albanian Tax Administration's own standing notice 'Njoftim per tatimpaguesit qe duhet te pajisen me POS/POI' states verbatim that by 30 MAY 2026 all taxpayers making cash sales in the listed activities must be equipped with POS/POI at every point of sale (accommodation structures, transport, public institutions with state capital); the deadline for ALL REMAINING BUSINESSES is 31 DECEMBER 2026. The same 2025 fiscal package cut the business-to-business cash ceiling from ALL 150,000 to ALL 100,000 (reported as applying from January 2026) and introduced a new ALL 500,000 ceiling on individual-to-business cash payments. Exemptions, verbatim from Monitor: entities operating in areas without internet coverage, those exempt from issuing invoices, and non-VAT self-employed individuals with no more than one place of activity. H1-2025 baseline: 46.4% of business-to-business invoices and 9.7% of value still cash; business-to-individual 90.6% of invoices and 64.2% of value still cash. CORRECTION: the researcher's law number 'Law 79/2025' could NOT be verified - neither the Monitor article nor the Tax Administration's own tax-procedures legislation index cites a Law 79/2025 (that index lists Law 86/2025 as the recent 2025 instrument). Parliament approved tax-procedures amendments in November 2025, but the exact law number remains unestablished; cite the DPT notice and the deadlines, not the law number.
verified_signals.source_name: Albanian Tax Administration (DPT) - 'Njoftim per tatimpaguesit qe duhet te pajisen me POS/POI' (notice 1942); Revista Monitor - 'Ulet kufiri per parane cash, deri ne fund te vitit 2026, te gjithe bizneset me terminale POS'
verified_signals.implies: The single largest terminal-demand event in Albania. Against 31,263 POS terminals installed at end-2025 (BoA via AAB, independently re-parsed this run), a universal obligation by 31/12/2026 forces a large incremental wave in H2-2026. Printec POS/acquiring: terminal supply, Android POS and SoftPOS for micro-merchants, key injection, TMS, deployment logistics, field service, plus merchant onboarding/eKYC for the acquiring banks. The 30/05/2026 public-institution leg additionally opens direct PUBLIC PROCUREMENT routes on app.gov.al that Printec can bid for in its own name rather than through a bank.
verified_signals.likelihood: Certain as a legal obligation - the 30/05/2026 leg has already fallen due and the DPT notice is live; the variable is enforcement intensity before 31/12/2026
verified_signals.followup: Establish the correct law number and Fletorja Zyrtare citation for the 2025 tax-procedures amendment (search QBZ by subject, not by number - 'Law 79/2025' is unverified). Quantify the residual un-equipped merchant base against the 31,263 installed terminals. Run a systematic app.gov.al 'njoftimi i fituesit' scan for public-institution POS lots (openprocurement.al's list endpoint ignores its search parameter, so this needs an operator crawl).

verified_signals.entity: Bank of Albania (regulator) - draft interchange-fee regulation
verified_signals.signal: The Bank of Albania has a draft regulation in public consultation, 'Projekt-rregullore per tarifat e shkembimit per transaksionet e pagesave te bazuara ne karte' (interchange fees for card-based payment transactions), transposing the EU Interchange Fee Regulation. 'Interchange' is the per-transaction fee the merchant's bank (the acquirer) pays the cardholder's bank (the issuer); it is the largest single component of what a merchant is charged to accept a card. Article 4 of the draft text states verbatim that payment service providers shall not offer or request an interchange fee per transaction higher than (a) 0.2% of transaction value for consumer DEBIT cards and (b) 0.3% for consumer CREDIT cards. CORRECTION: entry into force is NOT left blank as previously recorded - the draft Supervisory Council decision states 'Ky vendim hyn ne fuqi 15 dite pas botimit ne Fletoren Zyrtare' (15 days after publication in the Official Gazette), and separately that the regulation shall remain in force until the date of Albania's accession to the European Union. Adoption is conditional on prior amendment of the Law on Payment Services (law 55/2020), itself still in consultation and not yet submitted to Parliament, which Monitor reports may take several more months. Monitor reports current interchange averages near the 1.5% mark, with the all-in merchant commission reaching up to ~3% on FOREIGN-ISSUED cards; BoA projects the level could fall toward 1%, while banks argue 1.5% is the realistic floor.
verified_signals.source_name: Bank of Albania - draft regulation 'Per tarifat e shkembimit per transaksionet e pagesave te bazuara ne karte' (PDF, 12pp); Revista Monitor - 'Banka e Shqiperise pergatit rregulloren qe do te ule komisionet ndaj tregtareve per pagesat me karte'
verified_signals.implies: Interchange caps compress per-transaction acquiring economics, forcing Albanian banks to compete on VOLUME and cost-per-terminal instead of fee margin. That is the classic trigger for outsourcing acceptance: Printec POS/acquiring, Android POS/SoftPOS and POS managed services (estate deployment, TMS, key injection, field service) become cheaper than bank-owned in-house terminal operations. It also raises the payback pressure on every terminal deployed for the 2026 POS mandate. This is a margin/behaviour driver, not a scoped procurement.
verified_signals.likelihood: High that the caps are adopted as drafted once the Payment Services Law amendment passes; timing is the open variable and the amendment had not reached Parliament as at 22/06/2026
verified_signals.followup: Get the consultation closing date and the Payment Services Law (55/2020) amendment text - the BoA consultation index at /Legjislacioni/Akte_ne_proces_konsultimi/ 302-redirects to an AJAX page and exposes no document links to a plain fetch, so this needs an operator browser session. Then model per-bank acquiring P&L impact and take a POS-as-a-service proposition to Credins, Tirana Bank, Union Bank and BKT as the margin defence.
verified_signals.verifier_note: WebFetch returns 403 on every bankofalbania.org path, so I pulled the PDF myself with a desktop Chrome User-Agent (HTTP 200, 704,892 bytes, 12 pages) and extracted the text with pdfminer (pdftotext is NOT installed in this environment, contrary to what the researcher's access notes imply). verified_signals.entity: Bank of Albania (regulator) - draft law on payment systems and financial collateral
verified_signals.signal: A second Bank of Albania draft law is in consultation: 'Projektligj Per sistemin e pagesave dhe kolateralin financiar'. Its explanatory memorandum (relacion) states verbatim that full transposition of amended Directive 98/26/EC and Directive 2002/47/EC forms part of the EU accession Chapter 9 Benchmark. It transposes Directive 98/26/EC on settlement finality in payment and securities settlement systems (as amended by 2009/44/EC, 2010/78/EU and 2019/879/EU) and Directive 2002/47/EC on financial collateral arrangements (as amended by 2009/44/EC and 2014/59/EU), and additionally reflects EMIR (Regulation (EU) 648/2012) and related financial-infrastructure acquis. 'Settlement finality' is the legal rule that once a payment enters a designated system it cannot be unwound, including if a participant fails - it is the precondition for banks to safely settle irrevocably in real time. The draft creates a new, complete and consolidated legal framework for the operation, oversight and legal protection of payment and securities settlement systems, guarantees the security and efficiency of financial collateral and protects collateral-takers' rights if a counterparty enters liquidation, and repeals the existing settlement-finality and financial-collateral provisions.
verified_signals.source_name: Bank of Albania - 'Relacion per projektligjin "Per sistemin e pagesave dhe kolateralin financiar"' (PDF, 10pp)
verified_signals.source_date: Jul-2026 (retrieved; document itself carries no date on its face)
verified_signals.implies: Settlement-finality law is the legal precondition for the instant-payment scheme and for deeper SEPA integration. Participating banks will need upgraded payment hubs, ISO 20022 messaging and 24x7 liquidity monitoring - Printec transaction processing, HSM/security and managed services, plus AML/transaction monitoring capable of real-time screening (a 24x7 scheme removes the batch window banks currently rely on). This is a legal precondition, not a procurement in itself.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium-High: formal consultation stage and tied to an EU accession Chapter 9 benchmark
verified_signals.followup: Track adoption in Fletorja Zyrtare and establish the document's actual consultation-publication date (it is undated on its face; Revista Monitor has covered it, which would date the announcement). Map which of the 11 licensed Albanian banks lack a real-time-capable payment hub and approach them before the instant-payments go-live.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Pulled the PDF myself with a desktop Chrome UA (HTTP 200, 510,222 bytes, 10 pages) and extracted with pdfminer. Every element of the researcher's claim is present verbatim in the Albanian original: 'transpozimi i plote i Direktives 98/26/KE te ndryshuar dhe Direktives 2002/47/KE jane pjese e Benchmark te Kapitullit 9'; the amending directives are listed exactly as claimed (2009/44/KE, 2010/78, 2019/879 for 98/26; 2009/44/KE and 2014/59/BE for 2002/47); 'krijimin e nje kuadri te ri, te plote dhe te konsoliduar ligjor per funksionimin, mbikeqyrjen dhe mbrojtjen juridike te sistemeve te pagesave dhe te sistemeve te shlyerjes se letrave me vlere'; and 'shfuqizon dispozitat ekzistuese qe rregullojne finalitetin e shlyerjes dhe kolateralin financiar'. verified_signals.entity: Bank of Albania / Albanian banking sector - instant payments (TIPS Clone)
verified_signals.signal: Albania's instant-payments go-live is reported for NOVEMBER 2026 on a TIPS Clone platform (a licensed copy of the Eurosystem's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement service), superseding the earlier June-2026 preliminary target. The platform will go live across ALL banks operating in the domestic market simultaneously, will run 24 hours a day every day of the year including weekends and holidays, and is explicitly positioned in Albanian press as 'a cheaper alternative for conducting electronic payments at points of sale'. IMPORTANT SOURCING CAVEAT: no primary Bank of Albania document naming November 2026 could be found. The Bank of Albania's own most recent published forecast is the softer 'autumn 2026'; the specific November date rests on press reporting only, and one outlet attributes it to a statement by ECB President Christine Lagarde rather than to the Bank of Albania. The World Bank separately states that fast payments settling in seconds are expected to become available later in 2026 across Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Kosovo.

verified_signals.entity: Albania - SEPA membership and payment-cost collapse
verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 07/10/2025] Albania became operationally part of SEPA on 07/10/2025, when the launching ceremony of the first SEPA transaction took place at the Bank of Albania under the auspices of Governor Gent Sejko. The European Payments Council had approved Albania's inclusion in the SEPA geographical scope in November 2024, and all 11 banks of the Albanian banking system prepared and submitted individual applications (submitted 10/04/2025) to be operational from October 2025. The Governor stated that SEPA integration combined with the expansion of digital payments is expected to generate savings of around EUR 20 MILLION IN THE FIRST YEAR ALONE, comparing this to the Bank of Albania's AIPS EURO system, operational since January 2022, which has saved the domestic market around EUR 140 million. The World Bank separately reports that average business-to-business payment transfer costs fell roughly TENFOLD in the months following each Western Balkans country's SEPA launch, and that fast payments settling in seconds are the next phase, expected later in 2026 across Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Kosovo. CORRECTIONS: the geographical-scope date is 'November 2024' per the Bank of Albania, not the specific 21/11/2024 previously recorded; and the World Bank's EUR 2,500-per-month transfer saving is a single company's testimony that could not be confirmed as Albanian.
verified_signals.source_name: Bank of Albania - 'The Launching Ceremony of the First SEPA Transaction - Albania'; World Bank - 'Cheaper and Faster Payments: SEPA Opens New Horizons for the Western Balkans'
verified_signals.implies: SEPA plus instant payments plus interchange caps is a coordinated collapse in payment pricing across Albania. Banks lose fee income per transaction and must cut unit cost - which is the argument for outsourcing self-service and acceptance operations to Printec managed services. ISO 20022/SEPA message handling and 24x7 operations also raise the bar on payment hubs, HSM and real-time AML screening at all 11 banks simultaneously. This is the macro backdrop; the live trigger is the instant-payments go-live tracked separately.
verified_signals.likelihood: Already in force since 07/10/2025; instant payments the remaining leg
verified_signals.followup: Get the EPC participant register to confirm reachability for all 11 banks, and identify which banks OUTSOURCED SEPA message processing rather than building it - those are the managed-services buyers and that distinction is the only part of this signal with direct commercial value.
verified_signals.verifier_note: The researcher cited the World Bank feature as the lead source for what is fundamentally a Bank of Albania fact, so I went to the regulator. I retrieved the Bank of Albania press release by desktop-UA curl (WebFetch 403s on that domain) and it confirms, with publication date 07.10.2025: 'On 7 October 2025, under the auspices of the Governor of the Bank of Albania, Mr Gent Sejko, the launching ceremony of the first SEPA transaction took place at the Bank's premises.' A companion Bank of Albania release confirms all 11 banks submitted individual applications (10/04/2025) and that the EPC approved Albania's inclusion in the SEPA geographical scope 'back in November 2024'. I have promoted the regulator source to lead and demoted the World Bank feature. THREE CORRECTIONS. (1) The specific day '21/11/2024' is not stated by the Bank of Albania, which says only 'November 2024' - corrected. (2) The researcher attributed a 'EUR 2,500 per month' saving to an Albanian SME; the World Bank text is a single company's testimony ('our daily transfers cost around 2,500 euros less per month') and the page's worked cost example is Montenegrin, so the Albanian attribution is unverified - I have flagged it rather than repeating it as fact. (3) I ADDED a far stronger, primary, quantified figure the researcher missed entirely: the Governor's own estimate of ~EUR 20m savings in the first year, benchmarked against ~EUR 140m saved by AIPS EURO since January 2022. The World Bank 'tenfold' fall in B2B transfer costs and the five-country fast-payments expectation are confirmed on the World Bank page. Re-tagged [STANDING] with is_new=false: the triggering event is 07/10/2025, nearly ten months old, and the forward leg is already carried as a separate instant-payments signal. opp_size M -> Unscoped as a macro pricing driver.
